tide anchor drowned teal #237A6C

Something wet has walked inland: cold teal, bone, weed-green, and one warm rope-orange that does not belong to it.

Inspiration
Tidal mud at dusk, corroded bronze, drowned linen, the pale of things kept underwater.
Anchor
Teal sits opposite bronze on the wheel, so anything the Sea touches reads as foreign to the Palace world at a glance, and it holds contrast on both surfaces without going neon.
Rule bent
The accent partner is a warm rope-orange rather than a cool harmony, so that the Sea palette keeps one human colour to steal.

ash anchor cold ash #6A6E80

Deserters at a dead fire: cold grey linen, soot, dried blood, nothing polished.

Inspiration
Camp ash, unwashed wool, rust on a chipped spearhead.
Anchor
A cool grey carries none of the Palace's warmth, so an outlaw is visibly someone the bronze world has dropped; it still separates from the Sea's teal by having no green in it.
Rule bent
The anchor's chroma is below the rule's floor, so the status and accent-2 colours are raised in chroma instead of matching it, or the palette would be monochrome.

bronze anchor cast bronze #B8792E

Palace bronze in lamplight: warm, heavy, official, already tarnishing at the edges.

Inspiration
Mycenaean and Hittite palace goods: bronze, fired clay, undyed linen, bitumen, a single dark blue from imported lapis.
Anchor
Bronze is the setting's currency, weapon, graft and memory, and its hue survives both surfaces: dark enough to read on linen, bright enough to read on bitumen.
Rule bent
The dark surface carries more chroma than the rule allows (a trace of bitumen brown rather than neutral), because a neutral dark reads as modern.
